jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Arcade (Mobile)
jobs.description_text: Responsibilities: We're hiring a senior iOS engineer to be the technical backbone of the Arcade app. You own every part of the app except the games themselves: the wallet, matchmaking, cashout, onboarding, live multiplayer, and the compliance and integrity systems underneath them. Because we handle real money, our mobile problems go well beyond UI polish: real-time transaction consistency, fraud and integrity, and compliance that varies by state. Latency and reliability aren't marketing lines here; they directly affect user trust. You'll join a small mobile team (4 today, growing to 7+) where your decisions shape the architecture, not just the implementation. What you'll do: - Own end-to-end architecture and platform decisions for the Arcade iOS app, the foundation the rest of the mobile team builds on. - Keep the platform healthy: fast builds, reliable CI/CD, and a crash-free app, so product iOS/UX engineers can ship quickly. - Build and maintain the shared platform architecture that lets the game dev team ship new games into Arcade quickly, and that supports expansion into new geographies. - Build and iterate rapidly on features that move engagement, retention, and lifetime value: new game launches, live multiplayer, session depth. - Elevate the team's code and architecture through review, tooling, and design patterns. - Craft the mobile UX that makes Triumph feel like the best gaming app on someone's phone. Sweat the details: animations, transitions, and micro-interactions

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Rips (Web)
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Rips is one of the fastest growing apps in the collectibles space, and it lives on mobile today. You're going to bring it to the web. This is a greenfield build on top of backend systems that already work at scale. You'll own the web platform: the architecture, the conventions, the component patterns, the performance budget. The engineers who come after you will build inside the foundation you set, so we're looking for someone who has done this before. You'll be the first dedicated web engineer, but you won't be alone. Our engineers are deep in React already, and you'll be partnering with backend engineers who have spent the last two years building the systems you'll be consuming. What's missing is someone who owns the web surface end to end and has strong opinions about how it should be built. What You'll Do - Ship Rips on web, building on existing backend systems and APIs. - Set the technical foundation for our web platform: architecture, state management, build tooling, component patterns, testing strategy, and the standards that keep quality high as the team grows. - Own the user experience, not just the implementation. Motion, micro interactions, responsive behavior, and load performance are yours to get right. - Partner with backend engineers on API and data model design. You'll push back when a contract makes the client worse. - Create leverage. The patterns you establish should make the next feature faster to build and make it obvious to a mid level engineer

You'll have a direct impact on all facets of the business, applying your quantitative rigor directly to what drives revenue and player experience. You'll build the models and frameworks that power our most critical business decisions. You'd be joining a small, high-output quant team (4 people today) that operates more like a trading desk than a data org. We build the mathematical systems that power Triumph's core business: pricing engines, payout distributions, matchmaking algorithms, risk models, and player behavior systems. The team is led by a former quant trader, and current members left careers in quantitative trading to be here. The problems are as deep and interesting as what you'd find at a quant fund - constrained optimization, adversarial dynamics, risk - but with more ownership, faster feedback loops, and direct impact on what gets built. You ship something, and you see it in the numbers the next day. jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description_text: WindBorne is an atypical hardware company: we sell the data our balloons produce, not the balloons. Our customer is our own operations team, which puts engineering and the field about as close together as they can get. We push design changes to flying hardware roughly once a week while scaling production at the same time. Today every part of that loop is owned by full-stack engineers who each design a part, own its tooling, and tweak it based on field performance. That has worked so far, but manufacturing throughput and tooling maintenance have grown into a full-time load that can no longer share a desk with design iteration. This role exists to take that load. Manufacturing and Production turns engineering designs into repeatable, high-quality production. We build mechatronic hardware assemblies — PCBA, electronic sensors, ballast, and an adjustable inflatable balloon. Boards arrive populated from our suppliers. On our floor, we assemble the PCBAs into the electronics assembly, test it, and then build up the mechanical hardware, ballast, and balloon around it. The work is manual to semi-automated, and it has to hold together while the designs underneath it keep changing. We are running about 1,000 units a month and doubling roughly every six months. Most hardware teams get design lock before volume. We don't, and the manufacturing system has to work anyway. Own manufacturing engineering for parts as they come off the design team. jobs.description_text:
The Staff Security Engineer will identify security risks within our IoT device ecosystem, communicate those risks to management, and assist with the mitigation efforts.  This role requires hands-on experience with reverse engineering, networking, operating systems, and programming. The ideal engineer will bring these skills to bear on complex IoT security challenges. The Senior Security Engineer will also document security policies and procedures and ensure they remain up to date with applicable industry standards and compliance requirements.

Responsibilities:

The Staff Security Engineer primary job responsibilities include:

  • Perform IoT penetration testing, including firmware extraction, reverse engineering, and vulnerability discovery
  • Perform security research, analysis, and testing via threat modeling, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, and/or social engineering across a wide variety of applications, platforms and systems
  • Use a combination of manual and automated techniques to assess risks and circumvent security mechanisms of devices and application
  • Oversee and manage the deployment, integration, and configuration of security solutions and enhancements to existing IoT infrastructure and the enterprise’s security documents
  • Select and acquire additional security solutions or enhancements to existing security solutions to improve overall IoT enterprise security

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description_text:
About the Company

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense. 

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.
